group:paper-mock-jiangsu-nantong-2026-01.overview: 作者曾像多数青少年一样用手机随手拍照、发到网上给同伴看。翻看家庭老相册后，作者意识到照片承载着家族的历史，于是改用胶片相机，用心为自己和亲友留住重要时刻。
group:paper-mock-jiangsu-nantong-2026-01.fullTranslationZh:
像大多数在数字时代长大的青少年一样，我拍照全靠手机——一张张快照被分享出去，却很少再被翻看。我的 Instagram 主页是一组精心修饰过的这类照片，目的是给同龄人留下好印象。
从分享图片转向为自己记录回忆，这个转变并非一蹴而就。它始于一个简单的举动：翻看家庭相册。我被家族往昔的照片吸引住了。它们并不精致，却承载着文字常常无法传达的故事——关于生日、仪式和全家福的故事。在那些照片里，我看到了联系。我意识到，每一张照片都是某种更大整体的一部分：一段代代相传的历史。
正是这份领悟让我拿起了胶片相机。每卷胶卷只有36张，每张照片都需要用心，需要放慢脚步去观察身边的世界。如今我拍下最重要的东西：朋友的婚礼、假日和点滴的快乐时刻。如果一张照片没有拍成我希望的样子，也没关系。那些瑕疵成了故事的一部分。这些照片不是为了点赞或评论——它们是为我自己、为家人和朋友而拍的。
当我终于打开装着冲洗好的照片的信封时，会有一种重新发现的感觉。我被带回到那些时刻。从这个意义上说，我转向胶片摄影，就像是渴望重新找回把一段记忆握在手中时所带来的那份恒久与亲近。

theme.text: 照片的意义在于为自己和亲友留住记忆，而不是给别人看（they were meant for me, for family and friends）。
theme.quote: they were meant for me, for family and friends

冲洗照片时重温往日，作者明白转向胶片是想留住记忆。

completedSourceTexts.text: Like most teenagers growing up in the digital age, I relied on my phone for photos – quick snaps (快照) that were shared but rarely revisited. My profile on Instagram was a polished collection of such photos intended to impress my peers.

The transition from sharing images to capturing memories for myself wasn’t immediate. It began with a simple act: flipping (翻) through family photo albums. I was attracted by the images from my family’s past. They weren’t polished, but they held stories that words often couldn’t convey — of birthdays, ceremonies and family portraits. In those photographs, I saw connection. I realized that every image was a piece of something larger: a history that had been passed down.

It was this realization that led me to pick up my film camera. With just 36 exposures per roll, each photo required intention, a slowing down to see the world around me. I now take photos of the things that matter most: friends’ weddings, holidays and small moments of joy. If a picture didn’t turn out as I had hoped, it didn’t matter. The imperfections became part of the story. They weren’t meant for likes or comments – they were meant for me, for family and friends.

There’s a sense of rediscovery when I finally open an envelope of developed prints. I’m transported back to those moments. And in that sense, my shift to film photography feels like a desire to regain the permanence and closeness that comes with holding a memory in your hands.
